subject: Deployment model & secure-integration follow-up
messages:
From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@vertexhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andre Lowell <andre.lowell@vertexhealth.com>, procurement@vertexhealth.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — deployment questions and must-haves

Thanks for the demo earlier — we appreciate the clear latency/cost numbers. Following up with our security & infra asks so you can recommend the right deployment model. High-level constraints from our security review: 

- SSO: Okta (SAML 2.0) is required, SCIM provisioning preferred.
- Key management: all encryption keys for PHI must be customer-controlled. Acceptable options: cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys (AWS KMS with CloudHSM) or an on-prem HSM that can perform key wrapping. 
- Logging & retention: audit logs must be retained for 7 years and available for e-discovery/audit on request. Logs should be exportable to our S3 with lifecycle rules.
- Network: VPC peering or private link is preferred; vendor-hosted public endpoints need to be evaluated for egress controls.
- Compliance: must be able to demonstrate SOC 2 controls and provide evidence for encryption at rest/in transit.
- Data residency: US only (primary).

Questions we need answered to move forward: 
1) Which Redwood deployment mode (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) will let us keep customer-managed keys (cloud-HSM or on-prem HSM)?
2) Can Dedicated support BYOK with keys imported into our cloud account, or will that require Private?
3) What mechanisms do you have for exporting logs and configuring 7-year retention without vendor-side deletion?
4) Any blocking items for PHI in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

We can plan a short technical workshop with your SE and our infra/security team. Proposed slots: Mon Jun 29 10–11am PT or Tue Jun 30 1–2pm PT. Please advise who from Redwood should join.

Attached: Vertex-security-reqs-v2.pdf (annotated list of requirements).

—Jamie
Jamie Torres
Director, Cloud Compliance
Vertex Health
[attachment: Vertex-security-reqs-v2.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — deployment questions and must-haves

Thanks Jamie — this is very clear and helpful. High-level answers up front, then I list a few clarifying questions so we can land the right path in the technical workshop.

Quick summary: 
- Hosted API: fastest to production and lowest operational overhead. However, Hosted cannot support customer-managed HSMs that live in your account or on-prem; KMS controls are limited (we can encrypt with keys we manage; limited BYOK via our managed KMS is not available for Hosted).
- Dedicated: typically the sweet spot — dedicated GPU pools in our infra with isolation and stronger controls. Dedicated supports BYOK via cloud provider KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with imported keys or KMS keys in your account) for disk/volume encryption and model key wrapping in many configurations, but native on-prem HSM integration is not supported in Dedicated.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control — supports customer HSMs (PKCS#11 integration), VPC-only networking, and direct access to log sinks. This is the only mode that fully satisfies an on-prem HSM requirement and vendor-side-agnostic long-term retention.

Clarifying questions so we prep the right people for the workshop: 
1) When you say "customer-managed HSM", do you require HSM appliances in your datacenter (on-prem), or would a cloud-HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) hosted in your cloud account be acceptable?
2) Approx expected sustained qps and peak RPS for inference (so we size Dedicated pools / suggest baseline).
3) Will PHI (structured or unstructured) be passed to Redwood-hosted endpoints, or would you want Private by default for PHI?

Recommended next step: 30–45 min workshop with Marissa (SE) + Stephanie (legal/entitlements) + our infra lead to validate KMS/HSM path and logging exports. I've attached our deployment options brief for your review.

Available slots: Mon Jun 29 10–11am PT or Tue Jun 30 1–2pm PT (we can do both if you want separate legal + SE half-hours).

Attachments: Redwood-deploy-options-brief.pdf (short one-pager).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood-deploy-options-brief.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redwood demo — deployment questions and must-haves

Looping you both in — Jamie from Vertex Health sent their security requirements (see thread below). They lean toward customer-managed keys and a 7-year retention for audit logs. Can you help with two things before the workshop: 

Marissa (SE) — can you confirm the exact limits of Dedicated vs Private for: 
- BYOK: can Dedicated use an AWS KMS key in the customer's account with CloudHSM backing? Are there constraints around key usage (e.g., envelope/key wrapping vs in-process decryption)?
- HSM: can we support any per-node HSM integration in Dedicated, or is that Private-only? If Private-only, what would a PKCS#11 integration look like?
- Log export: what sinks can we send audit/app logs to (S3, syslog, SIEM)? Do we enforce any deletion policy server-side?

Stephanie (Legal/Entitlements) — if we propose a Dedicated + cloud-HSM (BYOK) approach with a Private fallback for on-prem HSMs, are there contract templates / SLA exceptions we should be prepared to offer for 7-year retention & e-discovery? Any redlines you anticipate?

I want to propose "Dedicated + BYOK cloud-KMS" as our recommended path if Vertex accepts cloud-HSM in their account; otherwise Private. We'll confirm in the workshop.

Thanks — pls reply with short notes or we can discuss live on the workshop.

—Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — deployment questions and must-haves

Marcus / Jamie — thanks for the clear ask. Short technical answers and proposed next steps below. I'll come prepared to the workshop with a short architecture diagram and a MAP template.

KMS / HSM:
- Dedicated: we support BYOK via cloud provider KMS when the key material is in the customer's cloud account. In AWS this typically means importing a key into your KMS or using a Customer Master Key (CMK) that you manage; it can be backed by CloudHSM. In that model, Redwood's Dedicated nodes will perform envelope encryption: we never have the long-term plaintext key. Caveats: some older model-serving code paths that do in-process decryption are not compatible; we can validate your model/workload in the workshop.
- On-prem HSM (appliance in customer DC): Private deployment is the only path that allows direct PKCS#11 integration with your HSM. We can wire the Private runtime to call your HSM for unwrapping/sign operations. This is not available in Dedicated.

Logging & retention:
- We can stream audit logs and application logs to customer-owned S3 buckets (or to a syslog/ SIEM endpoint) via an encrypted export pipeline. Once logs are in your bucket, you control lifecycle/retention — Redwood does not automatically purge customer exports. For vendor-managed log retention, we can set policy up to configurable windows, but 7-year vendor-side retention is expensive; recommend the export + customer-managed lifecycle approach.

SSO / Provisioning:
- SAML (Okta) + SCIM provisioning supported in both Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SAML but SCIM provisioning into a dedicated-managed org has constraints; we'll map these in the workshop.

PHI considerations:
- If Vertex wants vendor-hosted endpoints to handle PHI, Dedicated with BYOK + VPC peering can be compliant depending on contract assurances and network isolation requirements. For the strictest control and to eliminate any third-party key custody concerns, Private is the recommended mode.

Next steps / proposed plan:
1) Confirm whether cloud-HSM (CloudHSM in your AWS account) is acceptable vs requiring on-prem HSM.
2) Technical workshop (30–45 min): Marissa (SE) + Marcus (AE) + Jamie + Vertex infra/security. Proposed: Tue Jun 30 1–1:45pm PT.
3) Follow-up: we will produce a short mutual action plan (MAP) and an architecture sketch for Dedicated+BYOK and a Private option with implementation timelines and cost delta.

Attachments: se-notes-kms-hsm.txt (quick tech notes), map-template.xlsx (mutual action plan template).

—Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: se-notes-kms-hsm.txt (text, 3KB)]
[attachment: map-template.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)]
